invariants: The eighteen declared actual source/native provider observations must match independent literals; they are not full SQLite physical-schema or FTS acceptance.

Canonical listSnapshots exposes detached headers and source-qualified tokens. JSONL includes dev/ino/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs; the Windows change time must invalidate same-size rewrites even after restoring mtime.

SQLite tokens include physical store namespace, persisted store UUID, per-row incarnation and transactional revision. One nonempty append batch advances once; a failed batch rolls back events and revision together. Reopen preserves tokens and copying a store changes its physical namespace.
Lazy creation produces no stored snapshot; no-op append preserves revision; :memory: uses an actual isolated memory store.
Exact pre-abort is checked before backend work. JSONL stat completion and stat error check caller cancellation before publication or ENOENT handling.

Legacy native SQLite revision-column/identity backfill upgrades are atomic, preserve headers and retain incarnations on reopen. These are native legacy-format upgrades, not pinned upstream schema-19 migrations.
File-attribute handles are closed after success or failure; long Unicode Windows paths use ordinary extended-path syntax without modern OS patches.
identity: Logical snapshot tokens are scoped to the actual physical provider and stored session incarnation; eighteen paired observations independently assert stable/change/copy semantics.
ownership: Providers own persisted SQLite UUID/counters and temporary Win32 attribute handles; callers own cancellation reasons and detached returned headers.
ordering: Validate pre-abort, obtain one provider cut, check abort at each asynchronous stat boundary, and publish detached snapshots only after successful revision reads. SQLite writes and revision increments share one transaction.
errors: Preserve exact caller abort and native stat failures; only missing JSONL logs are omitted after checking cancellation. Failed native legacy upgrade rolls back DDL/backfill and closes the unpublished connection.
cancellation: Pre-abort and JSONL stat-failure boundaries are tested. Full provider epoch/FTS reconciliation and shared-task close/abort serialization remain outside this contract.
adaptation: Native SQLite retains its existing legacy storage tables plus identity/revision columns. The actual original provider and native provider are compared for declared logical snapshot behavior only; no SQLite on-disk interoperability or schema-19 certification is claimed.
open_questions: Full source SQLite schema-19/chunk/compression/foreign-database validation and cross-process power-loss behavior remain unaccepted.
All provider epochs, incremental FTS generations, two-attempt reconciliation, raw duplicate-artifact ordering and non-Windows physical birthtime qualification remain unaccepted.
